embedded_browser_surface_label: Example State official voter-information embedded-browser and constrained-container fail-open policy
delivery_role_note: Critical official voter-information routes remain readable and recoverable when reached inside an in-app browser, webview, or other constrained container rather than a full ordinary browser context.
public_read_in_constrained_container_not: The current official answer remains readable without first forcing the voter to switch into a different browser container.
open_in_browser_or_copy_link_note: When container behavior becomes the problem, the page exposes a visible open-in-browser action, copyable canonical URL, or equivalent first-party recovery path.
visible_canonical_source_identity_note: The page preserves enough first-party identity and source context that a voter can still tell they are on the official route even when address-bar chrome is weak or absent.
back_navigation_and_return_path_note: Back/return expectations are tested in constrained containers and the page preserves an ordinary first-party help route when host-app navigation behavior is confusing or brittle.
download_deeplink_multiwindow_recovery_n: Downloads, deep links, and new-context workflows fail open to a first-party recovery lane when the constrained container handles them differently from the full browser.
shared_state_and_sign_in_assumption_note: The office does not silently assume remembered full-browser session state will behave the same way inside every constrained container.
container_specific_failure_note: Known constrained-container failure patterns are tracked as bounded public-answer risks rather than dismissed as generic app or browser weirdness.
